verdict.rationale: Deel documents two credential types, API tokens and OAuth2. Its OAuth2 flow lets an app access "specific data" with explicit user consent, and its MCP server uses OAuth2 authorization for agent clients, which implies some scoped access for agents. However, the evidence never documents named scopes, per-token permission settings, or least-privilege controls for API tokens. missing for 10: an explicit list of OAuth scopes or permissions, documented scoping or least-privilege options for API tokens, agent-specific credential guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: It allows your app to access specific data in user accounts with explicit user consent, without requiring users to share their passwords.
Deel supports two authentication methods: ... API tokens ... OAuth2
Most MCP clients (Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT) handle the OAuth2 authorization flow automatically.
